comments.text:
On paper, the UK might look “poorer”, but our everyday risks are dramatically lower.
Americans earn more, but they pay more just to survive.
We earn less, but we’re protected from the financial disasters they face constantly.

Healthcare
We have the NHS - No insurance. No deductibles. No medical bankruptcy.
Americans can owe thousands for a single ER visit.

Annual Leave
UK workers get 25–31 days paid holiday, depending on the company. You’re expected to take it — no guilt, no drama.
Americans? Minimum 10 days, and taking time off is seen as disloyal. Many don’t even use it because bosses make scheduling a nightmare.

Sick Leave
We get statutory sick pay, often topped up by employers. Taking sick leave is normal.
Americans have no federal sick leave, so people work through illness to avoid losing pay.

Maternity & Paternity Leave
UK mothers: up to 52 weeks, with 39 weeks paid, and job protection. UK fathers: 2 weeks statutory, often more depending on the company.
In America? You’re lucky to get 2–3 weeks unpaid, and many mums are forced back to work within 3 weeks of giving birth.

Student Debt
UK student loan repayments are based on income, wiped after 25–40 years, and don’t affect your credit score.
In America, interest piles up forever, affects credit ratings, wages get garnished, and people literally die still owing money.

Housing Costs
UK buying/selling is straightforward: No escrow. No title insurance. Lower fees. Council tax is predictable.
America has closing costs, escrow, title insurance, realtor fees, and property taxes that increase yearly.

Home Insurance
UK home insurance is optional unless your mortgage requires it — and it’s cheap.
In America, even if your mortgage is paid off, banks, HOAs, or state rules can force you to keep insurance. You can’t just say no.

HOAs
UK HOAs are rare — mostly new-build flats, and fees are low.
America? HOAs are everywhere. They can fine you for grass length, paint colour, bins being 1 inch out of place…even breathing wrong.

Transport
UK has public transport because we’re smaller and denser - Owning a car is optional.
In the U.S., a car is mandatory, and with their fuel prices and insurance costs, it’s brutal.

Childcare
Childcare is expensive in both countries, but the UK is regulated and generally cheaper.
American childcare prices can be double ours.

Work Culture
UK work culture is more relaxed — breaks, holidays, and sick days are normal.
The U.S. leans into hustle culture: long hours, fewer protections, and less job security.

Minimum wage
UK is £11.44 per hour with strong enforcement. And it's increased yearly,  by law and usually above inflation. 
America $7.25 but some states are higher but this has been unchanged since 2009!

Food prices:
UK staples like eggs, milk and bread are cheaper and we have lidl, aldi, tesco, asda, NO TIPPING CULTURE,   but eating out is expensive
US - Staples often more expensive, eating out defo more expensive due to tipping culture and services charges,  prices vary by state and there are areas where you need to travel to find an affordable supermarket

comments.text:
18:47 日本に住んでいます。あなたの言う通り、ここでは何十年も前から少子化が進んでいます。

​日本では、3歳から5歳の子どもの保育料は、国の制度により基本的に無料です。親の収入制限もありません。 （※給食費、教材費などは月30〜120ドルほどの自己負担があります）

また、0歳から2歳の子どもの保育料は、親の収入（世帯年収）によって決まります。 

ここで重要な背景があります。現在、日本の0歳〜2歳の子どもを持つ一般的な家庭（最も多い層）の世帯年収は、約31,000ドル〜44,000ドルです。（※母親が産休や育休を取得しており、一時的に世帯収入が下がっている家庭も多く含まれます）

​この収入水準に対して、実際の保育料は以下のようになります。
・多くの家庭が支払っている実際の保育料は、子ども1人あたり月額120ドル〜250ドルの間です。
・国が定める最高月額（最高所得層の負担）は、子ども1人あたり約650ドルです。
（※首都の東京都では、独自の少子化対策により、0歳から2歳児の保育料も全員無料にしています）

そして医療費について 。
多くの自治体で18歳までの子どもの医療費が助成されています。私の住む市では、親の収入に関係なく、18歳までの入院・通院の費用がすべて無料です。
​（※ただし、公的医療保険の対象外となる治療や、個室のベッド代などは自己負担になります）

​日本にはこのような公的支援がありますが、それでも少子化は止まっていません。

皆さんの状況が少しでも良い方向に変わることを心から願っています。

A friend of mine had one.  He and his wife rented a building and converted it to their Day Care Center.  He bought a sprinter bus to pick up the kids from their homes (at an additional cost).  Once he was finished for the day he came and worked as an electrician at our plant, then after work he got the van and drove all the kids back home.  His business had about 40 kids at  $500 per week.  His wife was in charge of the center and they were making well over $20k per week (before expenses).  That was a million dollar a year business, and they were booked solid.
